question.text: An ATM call option typically has a delta of approximately:

answer.text: 0.5, meaning the option price changes by about half the change in the underlying
1.0, meaning the option moves exactly with the underlying
0.0, meaning the option is insensitive to underlying price changes
-0.5, meaning the option moves opposite to the underlying

explanation.text: The Logic: For an at-the-money (ATM) call option, delta is approximately 0.5 (workbook page 124). Delta is the change in the option price for a one-unit change in the price of the underlying, so an ATM call with delta 0.5 changes by roughly half the change in the underlying. For example, if the underlying moves up by Rs. 10, the ATM call premium would increase by approximately Rs. 5. The Trap: An ATM put delta is approximately -0.5 (negative), reflecting its inverse relationship with the underlying. Confusing the sign or applying call delta to puts is a common error. Note: The workbook example for an ATM call uses a delta of 0.50 to illustrate the sensitivity of the option price to the underlying.
